problem.h2: It's a familiar story, and it's not your fault.
problem.p1: A nice two-bedroom near Sol. Real-looking photos, a reasonable price for the area, and a landlord who's "traveling" and can't show it in person right now — but needs the deposit and first month by transfer to hold it for you. Then the money is gone, and so is he.
problem.p2: It happens constantly to people who don't yet know Madrid: exchange students arriving for a semester, people relocating for a few months, visitors booking a longer stay. They're the easiest targets, because they can't just walk over and check.
problem.callout: We're the person who walks over and checks — before you wire anything.

why.lead: ConfirMad sends a real person to check a Madrid rental in person before you ever send a deposit. We exist because renting a place you can't see with your own eyes is one of the easiest ways to lose money: close to a quarter of European exchange students report being scammed while looking for housing, and Spain logged nearly half a million cybercrime cases in 2025 alone.
why.b1_body: Not a photo review or a chat script — someone actually goes to the address and checks it against what you were shown.
why.b2_body: Online verification in under 12 hours, visits within 1 day, so you're not stuck waiting while someone else takes the apartment.
why.b3_title: Written proof, not just an opinion
why.b3_body: A clear report with photos you can keep, re-read, and show to whoever's paying the deposit with you.
why.b4_body: Checks start from €29. A deposit plus first month in Madrid easily runs €900–2,000 — this is cheap insurance by comparison.
why.b5_body: Just a real person on the ground in Madrid, working for you — not the landlord, not a platform's algorithm.

risk.h2: Nearly 1 in 4 exchange students gets scammed on housing
risk.p1: 1 in 4 exchange students surveyed across Europe said they had experienced a housing scam, and 21% of those who came to Spain.
risk.source_name: ESU/ESN, International Student Housing Report, 2023 (about 7,000 responses)
risk.p2: In 2025 Spain recorded 488,426 cybercrime offences, 72,217 of them in the Comunidad de Madrid. Most were online fraud of all kinds, not only rental scams.
risk.source2_name: Ministry of the Interior, via La Moncloa
risk.p3: One trick keeps working: a landlord does the viewing over video call — through an apartment that isn't actually for rent. A screen can be staged. Someone walking in and knocking on the door cannot.
risk.highlight: A deposit plus first month in Madrid easily runs €900–2,000. A ConfirMad check costs less than dinner for two — from €29.

faq.q1: What if I've already sent a deposit?
faq.a1: We can still visit and tell you whether the apartment matches what you paid for, but we can't recover money that's already been sent. It's always better to book a check before paying anything.
faq.q2: Do you check apartments outside Madrid?
faq.a2: We visit properties within the city of Madrid itself — even if your university campus is outside it, in Somosaguas, Getafe, or Leganés, for example, most student housing is still in the city. If the flat is genuinely outside Madrid, online verification is usually still possible — just write to us.
faq.q3: What if the landlord won't let you in?
faq.a3: That goes straight into your report as a red flag. A landlord with a real apartment and nothing to hide rarely refuses a short visit.
faq.q4: Is this legal advice, or a lease review?
faq.a4: No. We confirm that a listing is genuine and matches what you've been shown. We're not lawyers, and we don't review contracts for legal validity.
faq.q5: How fast can you actually go?
faq.a5: Online verification is delivered in under 12 hours. In-person and Live visits happen within 1 day of the landlord confirming a time, depending on availability that week.

check_tool.h1: Is that listing a red flag?
check_tool.lede: Answer a few quick questions about a listing you're looking at and get an instant read on common Madrid rental-scam warning signs — unrealistic price for the area, payment requested before a viewing, no video call, and more.
check_tool.privacy_note: This runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you type here is sent to us or stored anywhere.
check_tool.legend_landlord: What the landlord has said or done
check_tool.f_abroad: Says they're currently abroad and can't show the apartment in person
check_tool.f_transfer: Asked for a deposit or transfer before you've seen the apartment
check_tool.f_wu: Asked to be paid via Western Union, crypto, or gift cards
check_tool.f_novideo: Refused or dodged a video call when you asked for one
check_tool.f_rush: Pressured you to decide fast ("someone else is interested")
check_tool.f_lang: Listing or messages have odd spelling or grammar
check_tool.disclaimer: This is a quick self-check based on common scam patterns — it looks at what you told it, nothing more. It isn't proof of anything, and it can't replace someone actually standing in the apartment and confirming it's real.

check_js.price_severe_detail: That works out to about €{perM2}/m², well under the typical €{low}–€{high}/m² for this area. Unrealistically cheap listings are one of the most common lures in rental scams.
check_js.price_moderate_title: Price is a bit low for {district}
check_js.price_moderate_detail: About €{perM2}/m², somewhat below the typical €{low}–€{high}/m² for this area. Not alarming on its own, but worth a second look together with anything else here.
check_js.price_ok_detail: About €{perM2}/m², in line with the typical €{low}–€{high}/m² for this area.
check_js.abroad_detail: Can't show the apartment in person because they say they're currently out of the country. Legitimate landlords with a local contact or agency can usually still arrange a visit.
check_js.transfer_detail: Being asked to transfer a deposit or rent before you've actually seen the apartment is one of the clearest signs of a rental scam.
check_js.wu_title: Asked to pay via Western Union, crypto, or gift cards
check_js.wu_detail: No legitimate landlord in Spain asks for these. They exist because they are close to impossible to trace or reverse.
check_js.novideo_detail: A real landlord showing a real, currently-empty or currently-let apartment usually has no problem doing a quick video call to prove it.
check_js.rush_detail: "Someone else is interested" urgency is a classic tactic to stop you from checking things properly before paying.
check_js.lang_title: Odd spelling or grammar in the listing
check_js.lang_detail: Sometimes a sign of a copy-pasted or auto-translated scam listing — though plenty of genuine listings have typos too, so this alone proves nothing.
check_js.platform_title: Shared outside a verified listing platform
check_js.platform_detail_direct: Sent directly with no public listing to check against.
check_js.platform_detail_facebook: Facebook groups and Marketplace have little to no listing verification.
check_js.platform_detail_suffix: Easier to fake than a listing on a platform like Idealista or Fotocasa.
check_js.no_flags: No details entered yet that match common warning signs.
check_js.sub_green: Nothing here matches the usual scam patterns. That's a good sign — it doesn't guarantee the listing is genuine, but there's nothing obvious to worry about yet.
check_js.sub_amber: Nothing here is definitive on its own, but a couple of details are worth confirming before you send any money.
check_js.sub_red: This combination of details matches patterns we see in rental scams often. We'd strongly recommend not sending any money until someone has actually verified this in person.
